Other IISR figures: 21.6% dry recovery, 3.7% crude fibre, 7.2% oleoresin, 3.2% essential oil.

genetics_molecular_mechanisms: Sub1 gene (from FR13A, chromosome 9) limits underwater elongation to conserve carbohydrate reserves for post-submergence recovery. yield_research: The digest lists an average yield of 5.0 t/ha for 'Bahadur-155 Sub1' (rainfed shallow lowland, recommended for Assam). This name differs from Bahadur-Sub1 and the attribution should be confirmed. Sub1 varieties in Assam, including Bahadur-Sub1, showed a yield advantage of 1.0-1.2 t/ha over non-Sub1 counterparts in 2018-19 to 2022-23, including under non-flooded conditions. Sub1 introgressed lines showed no overall yield penalty under non-flooded conditions (general finding, not Bahadur-specific).

(2) AICRP 2015-16, Zone A: check grain yield 3116 kg/ha at 79 days maturity, downy mildew 1.5% at 60 DAS. (6) Jaipur district (Devla and Jharna), rainfed, 10 farmers: higher grain and fodder than local practice. (9) Customized fertilizer trial, Mandor (2019-20): plant height about 192.6 cm; yield response reported with other hybrids, no MPMH 17-specific yield value given. genetics_genetic_markers: Pusa 992 is included among the varieties in a 62K genic-SNP chip study. No marker positions or SSR details for this variety were found.
genetics_qtl_information: No evidence found for Pusa 992 specifically. The QTL mapping work found used Pusa Dwarf and H2001-4 recombinant inbred lines.
genetics_molecular_mechanisms: The 2025 BMC Plant Biology study of Pusa 992 under drought is a physiological and molecular study. It reports higher ROS and TBARS and lower proline than Pusa Arhar 16. No specific genes or pathways were named for Pusa 992 in the digest.
genetics_parentage_and_pedigree: Pure-line selection from the 90306 population (plain zone). A breeding table lists 'Selection from 90306'. The designation 'Progeny no. 11' is not confirmed in any retrieved page.
genetics_breeding_line_designations: The IARI annual report refers to 'Pusa 992 A', described as a short-duration A (CMS) line using a cytoplasmic source from C. The digest does not confirm whether this is the same entity as the released variety, so this is recorded with caution. No IET or AICRP codes were found.
genetics_breeding_method: Pure-line selection from the 90306 progeny, per the parentage evidence. No further method detail was found.
genetics_genome_resources: Pusa 992 is among the varieties in the 62K genic-SNP chip array study, which included resequencing of 45 diverse varieties. No accession IDs were stated in the digest.

field_trials: (1) Fertigation field trial, kharif 2015, Water Technology Centre: drip at 100% WRc with 100% RDF through water-soluble fertilizer gave the highest grain yield. The digest lists this under the Pusa 992 section but does not state the variety in the trial summary, so the attribution is not confirmed. (2) AMMI stability analysis (kharif 2007-08 to 2009-10): Pusa-992 was named among the best genotypes. (3) Intercropping and nutrient study (kharif 2015): Pusa 992 was grown with black gram, green gram and sesame. 125% RDF gave a slight seed-yield gain that was statistically equal to the standard dose. (4) Madhya Pradesh FLDs listed Pusa 992 with JKM 189 and TJT 501. The 1394 kg/ha vs 1078 kg/ha result applies to the combined varieties, not Pusa 992 alone, so it is excluded from Pusa 992 performance. (5) Waterlogging screen at the seed stage: Pusa-992 showed the least reduction among tolerant genotypes, with hastened senescence noted. (6) Pod fly screen: Pusa 992 was used as a check; none of 31 genotypes was rated resistant.
yield_research: The original record gives an average yield of 1643.00 to 2434.00 kg/ha. The digest contains no Pusa 992-specific yield figure. A 2016 review table lists unlabelled values (8.5; 145-150; 14-18) against Pusa 992, which cannot be interpreted. The IARI entry reports that Pusa Arhar 2017-1 yields up to 22.75 q/ha, 'considerably higher than the national check Pusa 992'. This is a comparison with a different variety and is not a yield figure for Pusa 992.

genetics_genetic_markers: Genomic simple sequence repeat (SSR) markers were developed from NL-97 DNA using next-generation sequencing. The analysis produced 2,183 contigs and 1,442 microsatellite-containing sequences from 8.8 Mb of data. A genomic library was also built from NL-97 using four restriction enzymes, with microsatellite-enriched clones captured. Individual marker names, positions and chromosome locations were not found in the digest.
genetics_parentage_and_pedigree: R-7 x RLC-4 (published on the PDKV Nagpur page, the PDKV Akola page, and a genotype trait table). Conflict: a PDKV Akola page lists "Seeta x RW-351" with the NL-97 entry, and the same page also lists R-7 x RLC-4. The digest does not resolve which is correct. The genotype trait table gives Nagpur origin.
genetics_breeding_line_designations: NL-97 (CSC and SeedNet); PKV-NL-97 (Akola and sowing-date sources); NL 97 (AICRP table). The digest treats these as the same variety. No IET or AICRP entry code was found.
genetics_breeding_method: Pedigree selection (as stated on the PDKV Nagpur page, which lists the breeding method as pedigree).
genetics_genome_resources: SSR marker development datasets derived from NL-97 DNA (next-generation sequencing; 8.8 Mb of data). No accession IDs were stated in the digest. No genome sequence or resequencing dataset for NL-97 was found.

breeder: Beena Nair, listed as Linseed Breeder and Incharge at Dr. PDKV, Nagpur (iior.icar.gov.in). The digest names no individual as the developer of NL-97. The variety was released by the AICRP on Linseed at the College of Agriculture, Nagpur, under Dr. PDKV Akola (pdkv.ac.in). The AICRP was based at Akola in 1985 and moved to Nagpur in 1987.
institution_research: LINSEED BREEDER, ALL INDIA COORDINATED RESEARCH PROJECT ON OILSEEDS, COLLEGE OF AGRICULTURE, NAGPUR.
contact_details: CONTACT DETAILS section in the digest: "Dr. Beena" (truncated). No email, phone or address was found in the digest.
field_trials: (1) Sowing-date trial with three linseed varieties: PKV-NL-97 gave 8.44 q/ha seed yield, below PKV-NL-260 at 8.85 q/ha. Location, year and authors were not shown in the snippet. (2) Nagpur-based sowing-date trial that included PKV-NL-97 alongside PKV-NL-260 and JLS-73; no NL-97 results were shown in the digest. (3) CSC record: NL-97 yielded higher than Kiran under rainfed conditions in breeding and agronomy trials; no numerical values were given. (4) Odisha powdery mildew screening of 294 genotypes including NL-97; no score for NL-97 was given. (5) ICAR-CRIDA contingency plan lists NL-97 for Marathwada and Vidarbha; this is a listing, not a trial result.
yield_research: CSC record: 588 kg/ha seed yield. PDKV Nagpur page: average yield 600-1200 kg/ha. AICRP table: 800-1000 kg/ha. These figures conflict and are reported as published. In a sowing-date trial, PKV-NL-97 gave 8.44 q/ha (844 kg/ha), below PKV-NL-260 at 8.85 q/ha.
stress_confirmation_note: The research summary gives a sowing window of the last week of October, whereas the official Seednet text specifies the 2nd week of October, and the drought level is rated medium despite no quantitative stress data.

field_trials: (1) Adaptive trial: RT-127 was the check; RT 346 yielded 19.4% above it (360 kg/ha at farmers' fields). (2) Rainfed conditions, kharif 2018: RT-127 ranked second among ten varieties for yield-related performance, behind only JCSDT-26. (3) Graded fertilizer doses: phenotypic stability analysis classed RT-127 as one of the most stable genotypes for seed yield. (4) Stability study of 15 varieties and advance lines at ARS Mandor: RT-127 used as benchmark. (5) Line x tester combining-ability study: RT-127 used as tester; the cross with VRI 3 gave significantly positive SCA effects. (6) Field screens: phyllody screen (minimum phyllody incidence, lowest leafhopper population); charcoal rot field screen in the USA (moderately resistant). Trial yield values beyond those listed were not found. The maturity discrepancy is noted: the AICRP table gives 82-86 days, while the variety record gives 75-84 days.

field_trials: (1) Chhattisgarh plains, kharif 2011, sowing-date by variety trial: JS 97-52 gave the most pods per plant (80.3) and the highest seed yield (about 52 q/ha) against JS-335 and JS 93-05. The highest yield was under a 20 June sowing, with a 10 June sowing at par. Higher radiation- and heat-use efficiency was reported. (2) North Eastern Himalayas, 2018 and 2019, zinc bio-fortification trial: seed yields of 1.87 and 1.69 Mg/ha for JS-97-52. (3) Weed study: JS 97-52 had the highest weed-smothering efficiency among the varieties tested, with maturity at 101 days. (4) Shading trial (35%, 50%, 75%): seed yield fell by 24%, 47% and 62% in JS 97-52 versus 51%, 82% and 92% in JS 95-60. (5) Maturity reported as about 100 days in the notified-variety table and 105-110 days in a climate-smart soybean e-book, so the stated maturity range is inconsistent across sources.
yield_research: Official recommended average yield in the original variety record is 2200-2500 kg/ha. The digest lists a yield potential of 2500-3000 kg/ha (from the notified-variety table and a commercial source). In a Chhattisgarh kharif 2011 trial, JS 97-52 gave about 52 q/ha (about 5200 kg/ha), the highest among the varieties tested. In a North Eastern Himalayas zinc bio-fortification trial, seed yields were 1.87 Mg/ha (2018) and 1.69 Mg/ha (2019).

(2) Salinity screen of 20 genotypes: LCA 334 highly sensitive to saline conditions. (3) Thrips tolerance evaluation, rabi 2022-23, Western Ghats agro-climatic region: LCA-334 gave the highest mean yield (133 q/ha), on par with RHRCH-10-2 (126.4 q/ha); thrips score not reported in snippet. (4) Coastal Maharashtra (Konkan) trial: early flowering, plant height 70.2 cm at harvest, judged suitable for Konkan. (5) Drying-method and chemical-treatment trial, Lam, 2003-04: method and chemical treatment effects on oleoresin, capsanthin and capsaicin were found; no numeric values in the digest. (6) Diallel evaluation (2013-14) of six parents and F1 hybrids for yield traits, including LCA 334; crosses selected on yield-trait performance. (7) Fruit rot and die-back data from the Lam trial relate to nutrient treatments and are not counted as variety-level evidence.
yield_research: Digest findings: (1) Organic and inorganic nutrient trial at RARS Lam, kharif 2003-04 and 2004-05, vertisols: the best treatment (green manure, neem cake, Azospirillum, PSB, burnt ash with 100% recommended N) gave 5397 kg/ha dry chilli.
